desc: Parse input; build list of bad intervals; derive free gaps (start, end) including [1, L_1-1] and [R_M+1, N].
Design reachability within a gap: sliding-window boolean DP capped at CAP = A^2-A+2B (Frobenius bound for consecutive denominations; long gaps with any seed have full tail).
Design transition across a bad interval: entry[d] = OR of tail[j_lo..j_hi] with off = gs - ge_prev, j_lo = off+d-1, j_hi = min(off+d-A+B-1, B-1), d <= B-off.
Edge cases identified: A==B (forced path, modular check), M=0, adjacent bad intervals must be merged (empty gaps), short-gap tail padding, N never bad / square 1 never bad.
Verify logic against samples mentally: samples 1 and 3 traced to Yes, sample 2 traceable to No; complexity O(M*CAP) ~ 8e6 ops OK.
Implement full Python solution (A==B branch + A<B gap sweep with tail propagation), reading stdin and writing Yes/No to stdout.
Stress-test solution vs brute-force DP on randomized small cases and targeted edge cases (A==B, M=0, adjacent bad intervals, unjumpable blocks, CAP boundary); no discrepancies found.
